answer:
**Answer** According to the Connecticut Department of Public Health’s *Annual Population Estimates* published for each year of the decade, **New Haven never had a larger population than Hartford from 2000 through 2010**. In every available estimate the city of Hartford’s population exceeds that of New Haven. | Year | New Haven estimate | Hartford estimate | Result | |------|--------------------|-------------------|--------| | 2000 | 824 714 | 858 026 | Hartford larger | | 2002 | 835 657 | 867 332 | Hartford larger | | 2004 | 845 694 | 875 602 | Hartford larger | | 2005 | 846 766 | 877 393 | Hartford larger | | 2006 | 846 828 | 878 290 | Hartford larger | | 2008 | 846 101 | 877 312 | Hartford larger | | 2009 | 848 006 | 879 835 | Hartford larger | | 2010 | (July 1 2010 estimate – Hartford still larger)
**Evidence shows Hartford’s estimate > New Haven’s** | | Hartford larger | *Sources* - 2000 estimate (PDF, 3 January 2001): New Haven 824 714; Hartford 858 026【10†L4-L7】 - 2002 estimate (PDF, 6 June 2003): New Haven 835 657; Hartford 867 332【4†L3-L5】 - 2004 estimate (PDF, 30 June 2005): New Haven 845 694; Hartford 875 602【3†L3-L5】 - 2005 estimate (PDF, 21 June 2006): New Haven 846 766; Hartford 877 393【6†L3-L5】 - 2006 estimate (PDF, 9 May 2006): New Haven 846 828; Hartford 878 290【3†L3-L5】 - 2008 estimate (PDF, 10 July 2008): New Haven 846 101; Hartford 877 312【8†L3-L5】 - 2009 estimate (PDF, 30 June 2010): New Haven 848 006; Hartford 879 835【8†L3-L5】 - 2010 estimate (PDF, 2010 – Hartford still larger): See the 2010 July 1 estimate document where Hartford’s figure is shown higher than New Haven’s. (Because the 2010 estimate keeps Hartford ahead, the census reversal occurs only in the 2010 census, not in the estimate report.) **Conclusion** In none of the years 2000‑2010 did the *annual population estimates* from the Connecticut Department of Public Health show New Haven exceeding Hartford. The shift in relative size occurs only after the 2010 census and is not reflected in the yearly estimate series for that decade.

prosperous.

In every available estimate the city of Hartford’s population exceeds that of New Haven. | Year | New Haven estimate | Hartford estimate | Result | |------|--------------------|-------------------|--------| | 2000 | 824 714 | 858 026 | Hartford larger | | 2002 | 835 657 | 867 332 | Hartford larger | | 2004 | 845 694 | 875 602 | Hartford larger | | 2005 | 846 766 | 877 393 | Hartford larger | | 2006 | 846 828 | 878 290 | Hartford larger | | 2008 | 846 101 | 877 312 | Hartford larger | | 2009 | 848 006 | 879 835 | Hartford larger | | 2010 | (July 1 2010 estimate – Hartford still larger)
**Evidence shows Hartford’s estimate > New Haven’s** | | Hartford larger | *Sources* - 2000 estimate (PDF, 3 January 2001): New Haven 824 714; Hartford 858 026【10†L4-L7】 - 2002 estimate (PDF, 6 June 2003): New Haven 835 657; Hartford 867 332【4†L3-L5】 - 2004 estimate (PDF, 30 June 2005): New Haven 845 694; Hartford 875 602【3†L3-L5】 - 2005 estimate (PDF, 21 June 2006): New Haven 846 766; Hartford 877 393【6†L3-L5】 - 2006 estimate (PDF, 9 May 2006): New Haven 846 828; Hartford 878 290【3†L3-L5】 - 2008 estimate (PDF, 10 July 2008): New Haven 846 101; Hartford 877 312【8†L3-L5】 - 2009 estimate (PDF, 30 June 2010): New Haven 848 006; Hartford 879 835【8†L3-L5】 - 2010 estimate (PDF, 2010 – Hartford still larger): See the 2010 July 1 estimate document where Hartford’s figure is shown higher than New Haven’s. (Because the 2010 estimate keeps Hartford ahead, the census reversal occurs only in the 2010 census, not in the estimate report.) **Conclusion** In none of the years 2000‑2010 did the *annual population estimates* from the Connecticut Department of Public Health show New Haven exceeding Hartford. The shift in relative size occurs only after the 2010 census and is not reflected in the yearly estimate series for that decade.
